learning_objective: 🎯 Unlock the secrets of the strongest shape! Learn how to prove if two triangles are identical twins (congruent) and explore their hidden properties.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: If you can place one shape exactly on top of another and they match perfectly (same size, same angles), they are 'Congruent' (symbol: $\cong$). For triangles, we don't need to measure all 6 parts to prove this!

We can prove triangles are twins using shortcuts: SAS (Side-Angle-Side), ASA (Angle-Side-Angle), AAS (Angle-Angle-Side), SSS (Side-Side-Side), and RHS (Right angle-Hypotenuse-Side). Note: 'SSA' or 'AAA' do NOT prove congruence!
An Isosceles triangle has two equal sides. A magical property is that the angles opposite those equal sides are also always perfectly equal to each other!

In any triangle, the longest side is always opposite the largest angle, and the shortest side is opposite the smallest angle. Also, the sum of any two sides must ALWAYS be greater than the third side.

fun_activity.title: ✂️ The Impossible Triangle
fun_activity.instructions: Take three sticks: one 2 cm, one 3 cm, and one 10 cm. Try to build a closed triangle with them. You can't! This perfectly proves the 'Triangle Inequality Theorem'—the sum of two smaller sides (2+3) MUST be greater than the largest side (10).

exam_tips: 📌 Order matters in congruence! If $\triangle ABC \cong \triangle DEF$, it means $A$ corresponds to $D$, $B$ to $E$, and $C$ to $F$. Writing $\triangle ABC \cong \triangle EDF$ would be wrong.
📌 Always use 'CPCTC' (Corresponding Parts of Congruent Triangles are Congruent) to find missing sides or angles *after* you prove the triangles are congruent.
📌 SSA (Side-Side-Angle) is a trap! It is not a valid rule for congruence.
quick_recap: ⭐ Congruent triangles are identical in shape and size.
⭐ We use rules like SAS, ASA, SSS, and RHS to prove congruence efficiently.
⭐ In a triangle, angles opposite to equal sides are equal, and the longest side faces the largest angle.
